patch.value:
## Rationale
25k+ history entries exist because item mutation paths call the history writer — but nothing proves coverage is complete. A new mutating command (or SDK primitive) that forgets to record history would silently break the full-proof guarantee that any item can be restored to any version. The contracts table already classifies mutating actions (register-mutation.ts wiring), so the enumeration is free and the gate cannot drift from the surface.

## Phasing
1. Item-scope mutations now: create/update/close/delete/append/claim/release/copy/restore/comments/notes/learnings/files/docs/deps/test-link/plan mutations/update-many/close-many/history-redact/repair/compact (audited rewrites must leave their audit marker).
2. Workspace-scope after pm-klo8: config/schema/profile/init/extension-state.

## Notes
- Assert via the SDK read path (history list) not raw file reads where possible, to double as an SDK-first exercise (pm-usfg).
- Explicit known-unaudited allowlist mirrors the eslint-suppressions ratchet pattern: shrinking-only.
History completeness gate: contract-driven test proving every mutating CLI/SDK action appends a history entry

The append-only-history invariant (all mutations leave permanent JSONL proof) is currently enforced by convention only; add a contract-enumerated gate so no mutating command can ship without recording history.

A test enumerates every mutating action from the contracts/register-mutation tables (single source of truth, no hand-maintained list), executes each against a sandbox workspace, and asserts a history entry is appended with correct op and author; item-scope mutations gate immediately; workspace-scope mutations gate once pm-klo8 lands (until then the test asserts the known-unaudited list explicitly so any new unaudited mutation still fails); adding a mutating command without history coverage fails CI; the invariant is documented in the history docs.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Live measurement of the two gate scopes, 2026-07-25, so the phased acceptance criteria can be checked against real numbers rather than an assumed inventory.

Item scope (phase 1) — 30 distinct ops appear across the 2,031 per-item history streams (34,160 entries total): comment_add 7,096, update 5,992, files_add 5,948, tests_add 2,759, claim 2,429, close 1,990, create 1,989, release 1,958, docs_add 1,243, test_run_track 733, learning_add 571, note_add 563, update_audit 309, append 114, plan_complete_step 85, plan_add_step 71, plan_update_step 44, history_compact_baseline 41, history_compact 41, history_repair 35, update_ownership_bypass 29, history_redact 21, plan_create_metadata 19, plan_create_initial_step 12, plan_append_discovery 12, plan_append_validation 9, delete 9, plan_append_decision 7, plan_approve 6, plan_link_step 4.

That observed set is the ground truth the contract enumeration must cover, and it is a useful cross-check in both directions: an op that appears here but is not enumerated by the mutation tables means the tables are incomplete, and an enumerated mutating action that never appears here is either dead or untested by dogfooding (which pm-pww8ax now tracks as a capability-coverage question).

Workspace scope (phase 2) — the mechanism exists and is barely used. `.agents/pm/history/_workspace.jsonl` holds exactly 9 entries, all with op `history:author-acknowledge`. No entry records a settings, schema, profile, init, or extension-state mutation, which confirms the phase-2 boundary this item already declares: workspace-scope mutations are today entirely outside the append-only proof, not merely partially covered.

Two consequences worth carrying into the acceptance criteria. First, the known-unaudited allowlist for phase 1 can be seeded from the diff between the enumerated tables and the 30 observed ops, so it starts honest rather than empty. Second, because `_workspace.jsonl` already exists and carries a hash chain, phase 2 is a matter of routing existing mutations into it rather than designing a new stream — which makes the phase-2 gate cheaper than the phasing note implies, and worth reconsidering as part of pm-klo8 rather than after it.

value.text:
Unaudited-mutation inventory measured on the shipped 2026.7.25 build, so the known-unaudited list this item's phase-1 acceptance requires can be written from observation rather than assumption. Method: isolated sandbox workspace, one probe item, each mutating command run once with the item stream and the workspace stream line-counted before and after.

Records history (item stream, 14 of 16 probed): update (title), update (status), comment_add, note_add, learning_add, files_add, docs_add, tests_add, append, claim, release, restore, close, and create on the copy target.

Records nothing anywhere (0 item-stream lines, 0 workspace-stream lines):
- pm focus <id> — mutates .agents/pm/runtime/session.json, verified by md5 diff over the whole tracker before and after. runtime/ is inside the gitignore block, so the mutation is neither recorded nor recoverable, and in a fleet the question "which agent focused what, when" has no answer.
- pm gc — completes rc 0 with no entry in either stream, despite being the one maintenance verb that removes data.

Workspace stream (_workspace.jsonl) carries only two op kinds after the probe: config:set:<dotted.key> and schema:add-type. pm-klo8 shipped the stream and enumerated ten workspace-scope mutations in its acceptance (config set/unset, schema add-type/add-field/add-status/remove-*, profile apply, init re-runs, extension and package enable/disable). Only the first two are observable, so the phase-2 scope is larger than the stream's presence suggests.

Not probed in the sandbox because they are package-owned and absent from a bare install: normalize and reindex both exit 2 with "Unknown command". Their audit status has to be measured with the owning packages installed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Unaudited-mutation inventory extended 2026-07-27. One addition, and it is the most consequential entry in the list so far.

Method: isolated sandbox workspace outside the repo with PM_GLOBAL_PATH pointed elsewhere and PM_NO_TELEMETRY set, running each workspace-scope mutation once and counting lines in the workspace history stream before and after.

Records a workspace history entry (8 entries from 7 commands):
  pm config project set ids_token_length 6   -> config:set:ids.token_length
  pm schema add-type Widget --folder widgets -> schema:add-type
  pm schema add-status analyzing --role active -> schema:add-status
  pm profile apply research                  -> profile:apply-types, profile:apply-statuses, profile:apply-fields, profile:apply-config, templates:save

Records nothing anywhere:
  pm focus            (already on the list)
  pm gc               (already on the list)
  pm merge install    NEW

pm merge install is a different order of severity from focus and gc. It appends merge-driver rows to .gitattributes, which is a tracked file, and it registers driver commands in git config. It is the mechanism the whole multi-agent branch story depends on: with the drivers absent, a merge of .agents/pm marks files as conflicted with no conflict markers and git add silently keeps one side. So the command that installs the safety net for concurrent agents leaves no record that it ran, no record of what it wrote, and no record of who ran it. There is no way to answer, from the history, whether a workspace was fenced at the time a given merge happened.

Two smaller observations from the same run. Every workspace-stream entry carries a null message, so even the recorded ops have no human-readable statement of intent. And this repository's own _workspace.jsonl holds nine entries, all of a single op (history:author-acknowledge), which means none of the config, schema or profile mutations that shaped this workspace were recorded here either; they predate the recording.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
The unrecorded-workspace-operation set gained its most consequential member. Measured on a sandbox tracker at build 2026.7.29.

None of workspace snapshot create, workspace snapshot list, or workspace snapshot restore writes a history entry - not on any item stream and not on the workspace stream. The first two are read-shaped and arguably benign. The third reverts item files and history streams to a content-addressed fingerprint: two items and three entries over two streams became one item and one entry over one stream, and no entry anywhere says it happened.

That places restore in a different class from the focus and gc and merge install cases this item already carries. Those write nothing about a change they made. Restore writes nothing about entries it removed. The full defect is now tracked as pm-6l2mza; recorded here so the presence census stays complete and so a future gate over "which operations must record" covers the snapshot group.
